what.heading: What is a loop?
paragraphs: A `for` loop runs the same lines once for each item in a list: each page, each word, each date. The indented lines under the `for` line are what repeats.

points.title: Count along
points.text: `enumerate()` gives a position with each item, and `range()` counts numbers.

points.title: Pair up
points.text: `zip()` walks two lists side by side.

points.title: Reset
points.text: A counter set to 0 inside the loop starts again for each item.

what.code:
for i, doc_type in enumerate(doc_types):
    print(i, doc_type)

example.heading: What it looks like
example.caption: The first time around, `i` is 0 and `doc_type` is "Cover Letter". Then the loop moves to the next box, until it runs out of items.

demos.label: for and enumerate
demos.note: The first loop gives each item. The second also gives its position, starting at 0.

demos.label: range and zip
demos.note: range(1, 4) gives 1, 2 and 3: the end number is left out. zip() hands you one item from each list at a time.

demos.label: Unpack in the loop line
demos.note: Each item is a tuple, and the loop line splits it into five names right away.

demos.label: A counter that resets
demos.note: count = 0 sits inside the outer loop, so every page starts counting from 0.

try.prompt: Count the words on each page. For each page, start a counter at 0, add 1 for each word, then append the count to `word_counts`. You should end with `[3, 2, 4]`.
try.starter:
pages = [
    ["Certificate", "of", "Quality"],
    ["Lot", "AB-4417"],
    ["Expiry", "Date", "2027-06-30", "Signed"],
]
word_counts = []
for page in pages:
    # start a counter, count the words on this page, then append it
    pass

print(word_counts)
try.solution:
pages = [
    ["Certificate", "of", "Quality"],
    ["Lot", "AB-4417"],
    ["Expiry", "Date", "2027-06-30", "Signed"],
]
word_counts = []
for page in pages:
    count = 0
    for word in page:
        count = count + 1
    word_counts.append(count)

print(word_counts)

checks.hint: word_counts should have one number per page, so 3 numbers. Append once per page: put word_counts.append(count) after the inner loop, lined up with it, not inside it.

The first page has 3 words, but your first count isn't 3. If every count is 1, count = 0 is inside the inner loop, so it resets for every word. Move it up one level, right under for page in pages:. Or check that you wrote count = count + 1 (or count += 1).
word_counts should be [3, 2, 4]. If the numbers keep growing, put count = 0 inside the outer loop. Also check that the inner loop goes over page, not pages.

try.stdout_hint: Your counts are right, but they aren't printed. Keep print(word_counts) at the end, outside the loop.
